Our Just Cause
At Hartsdown we are on a mission to provide an ‘Education for an amazing life’. Every day, we embody our STRIVE values – Scholarship, Teamwork, Resilience, Integrity, Vision, and Excellence – we use these values to guide us. We ensure that, no matter what, we help our students to pursue their ambitions.
We are a school that places the individual needs of our students at the heart of every decision. This commitment shapes our culture, curriculum, pedagogy and decision making every day; ensuring that every member of our community has the opportunity to thrive and make a meaningful impact: locally, nationally, and globally.
Being part of the Hartsdown family means joining a mission to create a better and more peaceful world; one where education is about academic success, alongside developing compassionate, kind, purposeful individuals who are ready to make a difference in the world.
Our Pillars
Academic Ambition
We challenge every learner to achieve excellence through a rich curriculum, expert teaching, and a focus on curiosity, resilience, and continual progress
Opportunity
We provide all students and staff with enriching experiences beyond the classroom that develop confidence, leadership, and real-world readiness
‘As much as possible, as often as possible, for as many as possible’
Culture
We build an inclusive, respectful environment where strong relationships, kindness, and high expectations help every student succeed

Computer Science Overview
The main objective of the ICT and Computer Science department is to provide opportunities for students to build key transferable skills in using IT. With these key skills, students can apply them to the rest of their curriculum subjects. This subject aims to expand the students’ research and communication skills, in addition to working on 3D design, programming with Scratch, Google Apps, Python programming, and build computational logic skills.
In Key Stage 3 students follow the challenging International Baccalaureate Middle Years Programme. This curriculum includes the basics of programming which pushes students to learn how to programme using Python. The thread of building transferable skills runs throughout Key Stage 3, where lesson outcomes require a mix and varied product to be produced. In addition to this we ensure students understand how to keep themselves safe online and how to use all of the key package features of key programs that they will use throughout their careers.
If students wish to continue ICT they have a range of options at Hartsdown.
Imedia is an exciting course where students get to develop and apply IT and design skills to real-world projects. They will learn to use commercial packages, such as Adobe Photoshop, Dreamweaver and Animate. This qualification gives an insight into careers in graphic design or product marketing. This vocational course is an excellent grounding for a career in creative ICT.
Computer science is a challenging course that goes beyond the usual ‘user’ approach which is ICT. Students get to understand and work with programming languages as well as understand how computers work and some of the ethical and moral components of information technology. This course is an excellent start for a career in computer science and progression to Key Stage 5.
At 6th Form at Hartsdown Academy, students can take their learning further and study the International Baccalaureate in Computer Science. This qualification entails students to study the application of IT in the real-world context. Students have the opportunity to produce a programming project that the students’ create to solve a real-world problem of their choice.
Computer Science Club
In computer club, students have the opportunities to go further, to advance their programming and IT skills.

Business Studies Overview
The course is designed to give students a sound understanding of business and the ability to use knowledge, skills and understanding appropriately in the context of international markets and the United Kingdom.
The Tech Award in Enterprise, is for learners who wish to acquire knowledge and skills through vocational contexts by studying the knowledge, behaviours and skills related to researching, planning, pitching and reviewing an enterprise idea as part of their Key Stage 4 learning.
The qualification enables learners to develop their technical skills, such as market research skills, planning, promotional and financial skills using realistic work scenarios, and personal skills, (such as monitoring own performance, time management and problem solving) through a practical and skills-based approach to learning and assessment.
The Qualification specifically covers: Exploring Enterprises, Planing for and pitching an Enterprise Activity and Promotion and Finance for Enterprise.
Outcomes: Students get better than average results in Business Studies and have opportunities to continue in 6th Form
Careers: Our students have gone to create their own businesses

Curriculum Intent
At Hartsdown, we place the individual needs of our students at the heart of every decision and therefore our curriculum is tailored to ensure everyone can be successful. We help our students make accelerated progress by ensuring we have an ambitious and robust academic curriculum designed to foster a love of learning and prepare them for the next steps.

Introduction
Hartsdown is committed to a high quality careers programme which ensures that students are well equipped to pursue their ambitions.
The careers journey commences from the very beginning of life at Hartsdown Academy with a diverse and focused programme for students that provides the opportunity to explore future pathways at key stages of their Hartsdown journey.
Creating a platform for ambition and aspiration to grow means students benefit from encounters with employers, training providers and further education provisions. Our links with local and national employers means that visiting speakers and exhibitors at our large scale events can offer their expertise and experiences of the employment and training sector, as well as being offered mock interview opportunities and first-hand experience of labour market requirements. Our links with local post-18 higher education providers (University of Kent, Canterbury Christ Church University and the University of Creative Arts) and post-16 further education providers including East Kent College provide additional pathway options for students seeking an alternative to sixth form or wanting to continue their studies beyond Year 13.
With the in-school provision of a careers advisor available at all times for guidance, students can explore options and ideas very early on, knowing they can access the support required to ensure impartial advice and informed decision making at all stages of their Hartsdown journey. Students also have access to our Future Ready online platform which offers access to wide ranging guidance and opportunities both internal and externally, physically and virtually, ensuring students, parents and carers have the most current information available.
Preparing students for their futures begins early on and a series of skills for life sessions are introduced during the KS3 curriculum with termly sessions that focus on developing characteristics and attributes that will become vital for future development.
Six sessions investigating our core STRIVE principles – scholarship, teamwork, resilience, integrity, vision & excellence
Five sessions focusing on the International Baccalaureate profiles – thinker, open-minded, inquirer, risk-taker, principled, balanced, caring, communicator, knowledgeable & reflective.
Four sessions exploring Skills for the Future, delving into the key requirements for the labour market, training and higher education including the beginnings of looking at University pathways, student finance and opportunities that can come from pursuing higher education post-18.
Whether it’s visiting a University in Year 7, receiving guidance for GCSE option choices in year 9, making applications for post-16 in Year 11 or applying for University & Apprenticeships in Year 13, students at Hartsdown Academy have the assurance of unequivocal guidance and support throughout their journey with us, exceptional access to employers and business professionals with a shared desire to share their experiences across all year groups and an exciting careers programme recognised for its achievements and efforts in developing student social mobility and widening participation.

English Overview
English Language and Literature offers students the opportunity to open doors to the world and participate actively in a global society. In English, we aim to inculcate a love of reading and to develop students interest in English literature, promoting reflection, analysis, empathy and cultural awareness through enjoyable, entertaining and stimulating classes.
Throughout Secondary, students are encouraged to read books and magazines in order to acquire good reading habits, and to discuss authors, characters and themes related to literature. They are also required to write at an appropriate level, so a dictionary is an indispensable tool in their study of the language. Oral comprehension and written expression, in different styles such as informational, persuasive and explanatory, are part of the linguistic objectives of the subject at this stage of education.
Additionally, students will read from different literary genres (poetry, fiction, and plays) and develop the ability to write different kinds of text analysis. They will study British works and authors belonging to the classic literary canon, the most famous representative of which is Shakespeare.

Geography
We support students to investigate and analyse the world around us. Using responsive teaching, scaffolding, and high-leverage teaching practices, we help our students to understand, interpret and critically evaluate the physical, geological and human impacts on the world in which we live, so that they can be well-informed, ethical and responsible global citizens.

History
We support students to make sense of the world by exploring how people, power, and events have shaped societies over time. Through studying a range of periods, places, and perspectives, students develop strong analytical, evaluation, and communication skills, while gaining a deeper understanding of how the past continues to influence the present and future.
